correctness.rationale: The announced complete-period and Haar theorems are sound, but the frozen scope section (line 23) asserts E_m(n)=O_n(m) for a fixed ordinary integer n under least nonnegative residues. The bound is false as written: for n=−1 each term is k−1, so E_m(−1)=m(m−1)/2. More generally any fixed negative n has n mod k=k+n for k>|n|. The linear bound is valid for n≥0. For the core theorem, with g=gcd(a,b), the uniform common residue modulo g has variance (g²−1)/12 and conditional CRT independence leaves just that covariance, including equal moduli and modulus 1. Sum the means and covariances and use the Jordan divisor identity. Möbius inversion gives the uniform summatory estimate x³/(3ζ(3))+O(x²) for J₂; summing against 2r−1 at x=m/r gives the stated cubic coefficient, harmonic error O(m² log(2m)), and tail O(m²). Haar level marginals match the complete-period laws; Chebyshev on the squares and monotone interpolation prove the almost-sure limit without independence. The recorded finite tests were inspected, not rerun; they corroborate the main identities, not the fixed-negative-input scope aside or the asymptotic theorem.
residual_risks: No assertion is made for short sampling intervals or limiting centered fluctuations. No repair is delivered: correcting the fixed-integer aside would not address the originality and value findings.
